topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's importance and acknowledges the difficulty of complement terminology before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Overview of complement activation and functions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes what complement is and how its activation supports immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions and historical exceptions needed to interpret complement components.

topics.label: C3 activation and the three complement pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 becomes activated and accumulates on a surface through converging pathways until complement reaches its trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement produces the effector responses that promote pathogen elimination.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic relates deficiencies in particular complement components or regulators to their characteristic clinical presentations.

topics.label: Staphylococcus aureus complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains bacterial complement evasion through Staphylococcus aureus and shows how one of its evasion proteins is exploited clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
